terminal.label: Terminal executable
terminal.description: Program name or absolute path, without arguments. Used by Terminal and launchers in terminal mode.

packages_mode.label: Packages — launch mode
packages_mode.description: Choose how your package application starts. Desktop entry uses its native Exec/Terminal settings; no package manager is required by this plugin.

packages_command.label: Packages — executable or desktop ID
packages_command.description: Your choice, not a fixed provider list. In terminal/direct mode: pacseek, pacsea, package-menu, gnome-software, etc. In desktop mode: an installed .desktop ID.

packages_args.label: Packages — arguments
packages_args.description: One argument per item, without shell quotes or expansion. For package-menu with yay: --aur-helper and yay as two items. Inactive in desktop mode.

monitor_mode.label: Task Manager — launch mode
monitor_mode.description: Direct for GUI apps such as Mission Center; In terminal for btop/htop; Desktop entry for native desktop integration.

monitor_command.label: Task Manager — executable or desktop ID
monitor_command.description: Your chosen monitor: missioncenter, btop, htop, etc., or an installed .desktop ID in desktop mode.

monitor_args.label: Task Manager — arguments
monitor_args.description: One argument per item, passed literally. Inactive in desktop mode.

show_terminal_arguments.label: Advanced terminal options
show_terminal_arguments.description: Show terminal argument lists. Saved values apply even when hidden.

terminal_args.label: Terminal arguments
terminal_args.description: Extra terminal options, one per item. Applied before run-program arguments; also used when opening an empty terminal.

terminal_exec_args.label: Run-program arguments
terminal_exec_args.description: Between terminal options and the TUI command: -e for Kitty/foot/Alacritty, -- for GNOME Terminal; empty for terminals accepting the command directly.

terminal_command_format.label: Terminal child-command format
terminal_command_format.description: Usually Separate arguments. Choose one quoted string only for terminal options that expect a single POSIX-style command string. Every program argument is escaped automatically.
